title: "Tracing Hidden Structure in Leukemia Gene Expression"
subtitle: "A compact, reproducible walkthrough of Ward hierarchical clustering"
format:
  html:
    toc: true
    code-fold: true
---

## The question

Can leukemia samples recover meaningful biological structure when the clustering algorithm never sees their ALL/AML labels?

This project treats hierarchical clustering as an exploratory lens. The labels are hidden during model construction and added only afterwards to interpret the tree.

## The analysis recipe

```{r}
expr_clean <- read.csv("../data/leukemia_train_cleaned.csv", check.names = FALSE)
expr_mat <- expr_clean[, !(names(expr_clean) %in% c("patient", "cancer"))]
expr_mat <- data.frame(lapply(expr_mat, as.numeric), check.names = FALSE)
rownames(expr_mat) <- paste0("P", expr_clean$patient, "_", expr_clean$cancer)

gene_variance <- apply(expr_mat, 2, var, na.rm = TRUE)
top_genes <- names(sort(gene_variance, decreasing = TRUE))[1:100]
expr_scaled <- scale(expr_mat[, top_genes])

hc_samples <- hclust(dist(expr_scaled, method = "euclidean"), method = "ward.D2")
cluster_assign <- cutree(hc_samples, k = 2)
```

## The tree

![](../figures/leukemia-dendrogram.png)

The two largest branches are strongly associated with the known leukemia labels, despite the labels not being used to build the tree.

## The expression landscape

![](../figures/leukemia-heatmap.png)

The heatmap shows standardised values for the 100 most variable genes. Blocks of warmer and cooler colour reveal expression patterns that help drive the sample hierarchy.

## Post-hoc label audit

```{r}
table(Cluster = cluster_assign, Cancer = expr_clean$cancer)
```

One cluster contains 27 ALL and 1 AML sample; the other contains 10 AML samples. The resulting 37/38 agreement is a descriptive concordance check, not supervised accuracy.

## Takeaway

The experiment shows how an unsupervised method can expose meaningful molecular structure. It also shows why visual separation must be interpreted cautiously: the cohort is small, the result depends on preprocessing choices, and no external clinical validation is attempted.
